messages.subject: Announce: Distance 3.5 Release 6 and D4 Beta 3
messages.subject_clean: Announce: Distance 3.5 Release 6 and D4 Beta 3
messages.body_plain:
Hi distance-sampling list,

I have uploaded new releases of Distance 3.5 and Distance 4.0 beta to the
Distance web site http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/

The new release of Distance 3.5, release 6, is almost identical to the previous
one, except that a minor bug with the install program has been fixed so that it
now installs under Windows 2000 (and hopefully XP).  So, if you have release 5
already, there is no need to download the new version.  There is a minor glitch
when installing the new release on Windows 2000 machines when Office 2000 is
already installed -- see the readme for details.

The new release of Distance 4.0, beta 3, fixes a number of problems, mostly
with the multiple covariates engine.  See the "resolved problems" list on the
web site for details, or wait for a posting on the distance-sampling-d4beta
list.  If you're interested in multiple covariates in the detection function
then you should download the new beta.

Both of these releases are identical to the ones we were using at the recent
distance sampling workshops, so if you were at the workshops, you already have
them on your CDs.

If you have any problems with either program, please consult the list of known
problems on the web page (under Distance Support).  If you can't find an answer
there, please email me.

Cheers,

 - Len Thomas

messages.subject: Re: stratification & global density estimate
messages.body_plain:
> > I have done a survey for dorcas gazelles in south Sinai. I have
> > tow strata in my survey. I am using distance 4 beta 3. The program
> > reports different global densities
> > If the density is calculated globaly it is 389 CV 31.9.
> > If density is calculated globaly as the mean of the density of the
> > two strata weighed by their respective area it 254.25 32.9.
> >
> > I would like to use z-test to compare if there is significant difference
> > between the two estimates. Unfortunately Distanse doesn't report
> > SE for the density estimate in case2, Is there any possible was
> > to get it from distance or calculate it manually?
> > I would appreciate any help.

Husam, the cv is simply se/estimate, so you can easily obtain it from the
results.  However, your 2 estimates are not independent, so the z-test is
not valid.  If the design was in two strata, the analysis should be
stratified - at least for encounter rate.  Otherwise, bias in your density
estimate will occur, unless either effort per unit area was the same in
both strata, or density was the same in both strata.

Steve

messages.subject: Re: Flying seabirds in DISTANCE sampling
messages.body_plain:
Falk et al.,

I have implemented similar protocol to sample flying butterflies.  While I
have not tried different protocols in the field, I have simulated line
transect sampling of moving objects.  I have contrasted counts (assuming
perfect detection) of objects that cross a plane perpendicular to the
observer (crossing the "beam") vs. counts that include objects within some
area in front of the observer (as in the popular "Pollard walk").  I have
found that counts of moving objects are always somewhat biased (a true
"snapshot" is not possible) and that the magnitude of the bias (it is
always positive) depends on the speed of the objects relative to the
observer.  It is a positive, but nonlinear relationship.  Furthermore, the
"perpendicular plane" protocol is much less sensitive to object speed and
generally suffers from less bias.

One problem that I anticipate, and could possibly be addressed in this
forum, is that  counting (and measuring distances) only when and object
comes "abeam" may result in excessive heterogeneity in detection
probabilty.  That is, one may first detect an object at a close distance
and follow it until it crosses the beam and some greater distance.  Its
detection probability is surely greater that objects that were first
detected at the recorded distance.

It seems to me that transect sampling of moving objects is an area in which
not enough attention has been paid.  I can't wait to hear more...

~ Aaron Ellingson

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Aaron R. Ellingson
Research Assistant
Colorado Cooperative Wildlife Research Unit
Department of Fishery and Wildlife Biology
201 Wagar Bldg.
Colorado State University
Fort Collins, CO 80523
a...@lamar.colostate.edu
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

messages.subject: Re: Model selection
messages.body_plain:
Hi Hussam, list:

I would guess that some, if not all, of your 4 results that look the same are
in fact exactly the same model.

For example, say you set up 3 analyses with half-normal key function paired
with cosine, polynomial and hermite polynomial adjustments.  Assume further
that you use the default method for choosing the adjustment terms in Distance,
which is sequential selection using AIC as the model selection criterion.
Let's imagine that in all 3 cases, the AIC for a model containing 1 adjustment
term is higher than the AIC where there are no adjustment terms.  In that case,
Distance will choose a half-normal with no adjustment terms for all 3 analyses,
making the results exactly the same in all 3 cases.

The bottom line is that it's important to look through the Results tab of the
analysis details, particularly the Model Fitting page, to see exactly what
model was fit.

Hope this helps,

 - Len Thomas

--

messages.subject: Request for photos
messages.body_plain:
Dear distance-sampling list members,

Many of you use Distance 3.5, and are aware of the photographs that liven up
the Project Setup and Data Import wizards.  As part of finalizing Distance 4.0,
I'd like to include some new photos in the software.  So, does anyone have any
digital pictures depicting distance sampling that I can use?  Suitable topics
include: wildlife photos, people doing distance surveys, sampling equipment
(binoculars, tape, etc), and sampling vehicles (boats, planes, etc).

If you have any photos that we would use, or know of any public domain
sources of suitable photos, please drop me an e-mail: l...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk
(do not reply to the list!).  Full acknowledgements will, of course be given
in the program.

Thanks for any help,

messages.subject: Announce: Distance 3.5 Release 6 - New distribution
messages.body_plain:
Hi distance-sampling list,

I have uploaded a new distribution of Distance 3.5 Release 6 to the Distance
web site http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/

The previous distribution would not install properly on some versions of
Windows 95 and 98.  This new distribution contains some extra windows support
files, and should (hopefully) install under all Windows operating systems
(except some non-English versions of Windows, for which there are other known
problems).

If you downloaded Distance 3.5 Release 6 during September, and found that it
wouldn't install on your machine, you should download again and try the new
distribution.  If you get any problems, read the ReadMe and let me know if
the problem is not covered there.

If you previously downloaded Distance 3.5 Release 5 or Release 6 and have no
problems with it, then there is no need to download the new distribution.

Cheers,

 - Len Thomas
